source: Lin et al. (2025) Sleep-time Compute: Beyond Inference Scaling at Test-time (Fig 3, non-reasoning models)
finding: On Stateful GSM-Symbolic, offline precomputation moves the accuracy vs test-time-token frontier at low budgets only. At high test-time budgets plain test-time compute is slightly better.
numbers: GPT-4o and 4o-mini, temperature 0. Sleep-time reaches baseline accuracy with about 5x fewer test-time tokens at low budget. At the highest budgets test-time-only slightly wins.
quote: test-time compute only baseline slightly outperforms sleep-time compute
limits: Authors guess the extra context distracts. Math problems split into context plus question, so the question is guessable from context.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: a crossover exists. Offline compute wins when budget is tight, loses when budget is large.

source: Lin et al. (2025) Sleep-time Compute: Beyond Inference Scaling at Test-time (Fig 4, reasoning models on Stateful AIME)
finding: With o3-mini, R1 and Claude 3.7 Sonnet the sleep-time frontier shift is significant. o1 shows limited gains.
numbers: Runs averaged: 3 for o1, o3-mini, R1; 10 for Claude 3.7 Sonnet (noisier). R1 budget set by the s1 budget-forcing prompt.
limits: Gain is model dependent. Only 3 runs for most models.
agent_relevance: Offline pass is not a universal gain. Check per model.

source: Lin et al. (2025) Sleep-time Compute: Beyond Inference Scaling at Test-time (Fig 5, vs parallel pass@k)
finding: At equal test-time tokens sleep-time compute generally Pareto-dominates pass@k parallel sampling on Stateful GSM-Symbolic. pass@k is called an unrealistic oracle baseline.
numbers: Parallel scaling applied only to the lowest sequential setting, to keep budgets comparable.
limits: pass@k assumes a perfect verifier. Equal-token comparison is only of test-time tokens, not of the offline tokens.
agent_relevance: Gap 1 partly: reuse of prior work beats resampling when the follow-up query is predictable. Offline tokens are extra spend.

source: Lin et al. (2025) Sleep-time Compute: Beyond Inference Scaling at Test-time (Fig 8, scaling sleep-time effort)
finding: More sleep-time compute (higher reasoning effort in the offline pass) keeps shifting the frontier. Up to +13% on Stateful GSM-Symbolic and +18% on Stateful AIME at similar test-time budget.
numbers: Figure 8 and text; o1, o3-mini, R1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet.
limits: Total spend (sleep plus test) rises. Not equal-total-token.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: offline gains are paid for with extra tokens, so equal-total-token superiority is not shown.

source: Lin et al. (2025) Sleep-time Compute: Beyond Inference Scaling at Test-time (Sec 5.4, query predictability)
finding: The accuracy gap between sleep-time and test-time-only widens as the question becomes more predictable from the context (five predictability bins, GPT-4o-mini, Verbosity 0).
numbers: Predictability scored by a language-model likelihood. Both GSM-Symbolic P1 and P2 show the trend.
limits: Correlational. Predictability is scored on benchmark questions built from context.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: for unpredictable queries the offline benefit shrinks. This answers the question mostly in the negative for unpredictable queries.

source: Lin et al. (2025) Sleep-time Compute: Beyond Inference Scaling at Test-time (Sec 6, SWE-Features agentic case study)
finding: On a new multi-file feature benchmark (F1 of predicted modified files) sleep-time helps at low test-time budget (about 1.5x fewer tokens) but test-time-only is better at high budget, with higher precision.
numbers: Agent that explored the repo offline edited more files, so lower precision. Metric is file-set F1, not passing tests.
limits: Authors' own benchmark. Proxy metric. Single case study.
agent_relevance: Gap 3: the crossover on agentic tasks sits at a modest test-time budget.

source: Ghosal et al. (2025) Does Thinking More Always Help? (parallel thinking at 16K)
finding: At a fixed 16K-token budget, splitting tokens over independent traces plus majority vote beats extending one trace with Wait / Think more.
numbers: Up to 22% higher accuracy than 'Wait & Think More' and about 47% higher than exact-thinking budget control (Fig 8). Three models; GSM-8K, MATH-500, AIME 2024.
quote: parallel thinking consistently maintains or enhances accuracy with increasing thinking budget
limits: Majority vote needs a voteable answer. Not tested on open-ended or insight tasks.
agent_relevance: Gap 5 and 1: at equal tokens independent restarts beat Wait continuation on math. Not tested on lateral thinking.

source: Ghosal et al. (2025) Does Thinking More Always Help? (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B on GSM-8K)
finding: Concrete case of sequential extension hurting: raising budget from 385 tokens to 16000 with Wait & Think More lowered accuracy. Same budget in parallel raised it.
numbers: -11.8% for Wait & Think More vs +10.1% for parallel thinking, relative to standard thinking.
limits: Small distilled model, easy benchmark. Likely a worst case.
agent_relevance: A continued-thought step needs a stop rule. Fresh restarts avoid anchoring on a bad trace.

source: Jiang et al. (2023) BRAINTEASER: Lateral Thinking Puzzles for LLMs
finding: Benchmark of 1,100 lateral-thinking puzzles. Best model (ChatGPT) is far under humans. The gap widens when consistency across semantic and context rewrites is required.
numbers: ChatGPT 53% (sentence puzzles) and 63% (word puzzles). Humans 92% (102 sampled items, three expert annotators). Random 25%.
limits: 2023 models. No test of Wait, restarts or incubation steps in this paper.
agent_relevance: Gap 5: base rates only. No evidence yet that continuation or restarts help here. Gap stays open.

source: Jiang et al. (2024) SemEval-2024 Task 9: BRAINTEASER
finding: Shared-task overview. Abstract gives participation only and says the task needs defying commonsense associations.
numbers: 483 team submissions from 182 participants over two subtasks. No scores in the abstract.
limits: Only abstract opened. Per-system methods (any sampling or reflection) not read.
agent_relevance: Gap 5: a follow-up read of system papers could show whether restarts or long reasoning won.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet (oracle vs intrinsic)
finding: With oracle correctness labels self-correction helps a lot. Without them it does not. So the gain comes from knowing when the first answer is wrong.
numbers: With oracle labels GPT-4 on GSM8K reaches 95.5 to 97.5 (from 84.3 standard); HotpotQA GPT-4 29.0 to 49.0 and 59.0. Table text was garbled in extraction, so read these as approximate.
limits: Table layout broke in pdftotext. Intrinsic-table numbers not re-read here.
agent_relevance: Gap 9: an impasse detector is the whole benefit. Without a cheap reliable one, a return-after-break step cannot be targeted.

source: Huang et al. (2024) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet (answer-change analysis)
finding: On GSM8K GPT-3.5 keeps its first answer 74.7% of the time over two self-correction rounds. When it does change, it more often turns a right answer wrong than a wrong one right.
numbers: 74.7% retained (GPT-3.5, GSM8K). CommonSenseQA answers change more often because wrong options look plausible.
limits: One model and two datasets in this analysis.
agent_relevance: Gap 9: models do not judge their own correctness, so confidence-based impasse triggers are weak.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion (resampling does not rescue failed tasks)
finding: On HotPotQA, ReAct-only, CoT-only and CoT(GT)-only baselines at temperature 0.7 solved none of the tasks they failed first time in later trials. Reflexion agents did.
numbers: No failed first-trial task was solved by later baseline trials. Reflexion with CoT(GT) gained 14% absolute without ground truth. ALFWorld 130 of 134 tasks in 12 trials; ReAct-only stalled between trials 6 and 7.
limits: Retries are not equal-token. Reflexion adds reflection text and memory. The statement is about this setup, not a general law.
agent_relevance: Gap 1: plain resampling from scratch can stall on failed items. A return step that carries a short note about the failure beat it here.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion (ablation, reflection vs episodic memory)
finding: Adding the last trajectory alone (episodic memory) helps less than adding a first-person written self-reflection.
numbers: Self-reflection adds an 8% absolute boost over the episodic-memory-only variant (HotPotQA, CoT(GT) base).
limits: Single dataset. Ablation on one base setup.
agent_relevance: Gap 1 and 2: carrying a distilled lesson works better than carrying the full failed context. This is the closest LLM echo of forgetting a misleading context.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion (no unit tests ablation)
finding: Self-reflection without an external test hurt. The agent cannot tell if its implementation is correct and makes harmful edits.
numbers: HumanEval Rust, 50 hardest problems, GPT-4: 52% without test generation vs 60% baseline.
agent_relevance: Gap 9: returning to a problem needs an external signal that the problem is still unsolved.

source: Gema et al. (2025) Inverse Scaling in Test-Time Compute
finding: Longer reasoning lowers accuracy on four task families. Claude models get distracted by irrelevant information; OpenAI o-series overfit to framing; models drift to spurious correlations and lose focus on deduction.
numbers: Four categories: counting with distractors, regression with spurious features, deduction with constraint tracking, AI-risk evaluations. No numbers in the abstract.
agent_relevance: Gap 2: long-context anchoring is a real LLM fixation. Resetting context is a plausible fix, not tested here.

source: Marjanovic et al. (2025) Thoughtology: DeepSeek-R1 reasoning
finding: R1 tends to ruminate on previously explored problem formulations, which blocks exploring new ones. The paper also reports a sweet spot of thought length.
limits: Abstract only. The word 'fixation' is not used. The analogy to Ward and Smith is mine.
agent_relevance: Gap 2: rumination on an old formulation is a direct analogue of fixation, so dropping the old formulation (not just resting) is the test to run.

source: Muennighoff et al. (2025) s1: Simple test-time scaling
finding: Budget forcing appends Wait when the model tries to stop. The abstract says this often makes the model double-check and fix wrong steps.
numbers: AIME24 50% to 57% with budget forcing on s1-32B.
limits: Abstract only. No parallel vs sequential comparison on this page; Ghosal d07 gives it.
agent_relevance: Gap 5: positive for Wait continuation on math, set against d07 and d08.

source: Sio and Ormerod (2009) Does incubation enhance problem solving? Psychological Bulletin 135(1), 94-120
finding: Not read in full. Crossref lists the publisher PDF only for similarity checking, and the DOI redirects to the paywalled APA page. Weighted vs unweighted mean d is therefore still unverified.
limits: Publisher full text not reachable this session. No open copy found on the Lancaster repository list.
agent_relevance: Gap 4 stays open. Keep K02 as a range of 0.29 to 0.41.
